svg.title: Dependency updates flow through the framework, not around it: A generated project gets its tool updates inside the toolbox update, and the toolbox updates each tool on its own
svg.text: Dependency updates flow through the framework, not around
Scenario: A generated project gets its tool updates inside the toolbox update, and the toolbox updates each
A generated project only receives the toolbox update
The toolbox updates its own tools, one merge request each

g.text: Given the project deploys its own image, pinned at 0.2.0 in its staging manifest
Off camera, the test GitLab holds a copy of the toolbox with two releases. Release 1.0.0 pins node 22.0.0 and glab
1.40.0, and release 1.0.1 moves them to 22.1.0 and 1.41.0. Next to it sits a project generated from release 1.0.0, whose
developer added one dependency of their own: toml 0.10.0 in project/requirements.txt.
The project also deploys its own image. GitLab shows project/kustomize/overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml, the file
that says which version runs in staging: it pins that image at 0.2.0. The project's registry already holds 0.2.1. For
the test, that registry is a small stand-in at localhost:5050 that knows these two versions.
When Renovate runs on a project generated from an older toolbox release, it opens only the
toolbox update and the toml update
Renovate runs on that project. GitLab's list of open merge requests shows two of them, "update dependency toml to
v0.10.2" and "update devsecops toolbox to v1.0.1", and neither carries a red failed check. There is none for node or
glab, although the project still pins them old: those tools belong to the toolbox.
There is none for the project's own image either, and Renovate never asks the registry about it. A Renovate bump of that
image was a fix commit, so it made a release, the release published a new image, and Renovate bumped it again, in a
loop. A version reaches staging through a merge request a person opens.
Then the toolbox update brings the newer tool pins with it, and no stray VERSION file
The Changes tab of the toolbox update. Renovate ran the toolbox's own update command for it, from the project root and
without a shell. The merge request holds what that command changed: the answers file now names release 1.0.1, and node
and glab move to the pins release 1.0.1 carries.
No .config/devsecops/VERSION is among the files. That stray file is what Renovate's own Copier run used to leave,
working from the folder of the answers file.
When the toolbox's own Renovate runs, it opens one merge request per dependency
Off camera, the toolbox's main branch gets one more commit after both releases. It pins five dependencies back to old
versions: copier and ansible-core from Python, playwright from npm, the Playwright test image from the Microsoft
registry, and MegaLinter, whose number is a Docker tag.
Renovate runs on the toolbox itself. For the test, a setting limits it to these five and holds each one to a single
newer release, so the picture never moves. GitLab lists five merge requests, one per dependency: when twenty updates
ride in one merge request, one broken package holds the nineteen others back.
The playwright package and its test image come in two merge requests, because npm publishes first and the image follows
days later. That is why the test image installs the browser its own playwright asks for.
Then the copier update moves its config pin and its installer pin together
The Changes tab of the copier update. copier is pinned in two places: .config/copier/requirements.txt, and install.sh,
which installs copier before the toolbox is on the machine. Both move from 9.0.1 to 9.1.0 in this one merge request.
Before the pin-back, the test checks that every install.sh pin equals its .config source, for task, copier, gum and
glow.
And the MegaLinter update moves the local pin and both CI pins together
The Changes tab of the MegaLinter update. The local runner in .config/megalinter/package.json and the image of both CI
templates move from 9.1.0 to 9.5.0 together, so a local run and the pipeline never lint with two versions.
9.5.0 only exists on ghcr.io, because Docker Hub stopped at 9.4.0. Renovate reads the registry that still publishes.
